summary: Today's health-tech landscape shows significant movement on drug pricing policy, senior care innovation, and healthcare infrastructure challenges. An analysis warns that Trump's "most-favored nation" pricing initiative could deliver far less savings than projected if pharma companies exploit secretive deal arrangements to circumvent the policy. On the access front, Interra Health is now helping Medicare patients obtain GLP-1 medications through a new Bridge program at $50 monthly, while Inspiren secured $70 million in Series C funding to scale its AI platform for senior living facilities, which uses ambient sensors and computer vision to predict falls before they occur. Meanwhile, McKesson disclosed a cybersecurity incident involving data exfiltration, underscoring ongoing security vulnerabilities in healthcare infrastructure. The broader challenge facing the sector is that healthcare software must grapple with operational complexity that extends beyond user interface design—vendors need solutions that handle the messy realities of modern care environments rather than idealized workflows.
